headline: Two applicants to Seoul universities were caught cheating in entrance exams with AI glasses, which they swapped in for ordinary glasses once the tests began.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a clear first-of-its-kind exam cheating case reported by several Korean outlets, though small in number and the Korea Times names no sources.
importance_line: Test-takers and universities running high-stakes exams are affected first, with Yonsei still deciding a penalty while the University of Seoul has already banned its applicant for three years, but only two cases are known and the Korea Times cites unnamed sources.
summary: The Korea Times reports, citing unnamed sources, that two college applicants were caught this month wearing banned AI glasses in entrance exams at two Seoul universities: an applicant at Yonsei University who switched from normal glasses to AI glasses after the mathematics essay exam began on Saturday, and an applicant at the University of Seoul who did the same on 3 October. The University of Seoul removed its applicant from the exam and banned the applicant from its entrance exams for three years, while Yonsei is still reviewing possible action against its student.
notes: Korea Times text read in full (short). The cases are also reported by Korea JoongAng Daily (13 Oct, first known case of its kind in Korea) and The Korea Herald (14 Oct), which dates the Yonsei exam Friday where the others say Saturday 10 Oct. The events were 3 and 10 Oct but first reported on 12-13 Oct, so treated as new.
